A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flow of Reasoning by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on BlocksWorld, Game24, and PrOntoQA, including component ablations, sensitivity studies, and generated examples.

after.justification: V3 reports original experiments on five tasks, expanded ablations, and appendix results measuring training costs and trajectory probabilities.

M1.justification: V1 restricts reasoning to trees with backward probability PB=1. V3 Sections 3.1–3.2 allow merged paths in DAGs and use PB=1/|Pa(s)| in the objective. V3 also introduces task-specific rewards based on remaining solution distance for Rubik's Cube and Hamming-distance reductions for 1D-ARC. The log-variance loss and random-policy local search already appeared in v1's appendices.

E1.justification: V3 retains BlocksWorld, Game24, and PrOntoQA and adds spatial planning with a 2x2 Rubik's Cube and transformation-program induction on 1D-ARC. The latter covers movement, filling, and denoising tasks. These additions introduce distinct data and reasoning requirements.

E2.justification: BlocksWorld Table 1 adds SFT with diverse beam, nucleus, and typical sampling, SFT+GFN-CoT, and o1-mini/o1-preview. Game24 Table 2 adds XoT, GPT-4o CoT, and o1-mini; PrOntoQA adds GPT-4o CoT. The new tasks also evaluate GoT and IO/program-only/hypothesis-search comparators. GFN-CoT's source was cited in v1, but its evaluated comparison is new.

E3.justification: V3 introduces creativity as an evaluation metric. The reported BlocksWorld training budget changes from 20 to 10 iterations (v1 Appendix B.2; v3 Appendix C.4). Game24's test selection changes from 100 randomly selected examples to difficulty-ordered indices 910–1010, and the 100-sample condition disappears. These are reported protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 Table 6 adds replay-buffer and epsilon-sampling ablations alongside the retained local-search and reward ablations. It adds a training-cost comparison, a two-trajectory probability check, and a comparative Game24 case study (Tables 7–8 and Figure 1). V1's Game24 100-sample sensitivity result is removed. The existing reward-weight and data-efficiency analyses remain in Figure 3.

E5.justification: V1 supplies no repeated-run counts or result uncertainty. V3 Section 4.1 introduces three-repetition reporting, with means and standard deviations for FOR and many baselines and ablations, subject to stated cost-based exceptions. Creativity uses one repetition, and training times average three runs. This establishes new reporting rather than an increase from a known v1 run count.

E6.justification: V3 adds creativity scores and results including FOR accuracies of 10.87% on Rubik's Cube and 50.37% on 1D-ARC. Six-step BlocksWorld accuracy changes from 71.71% to 78.44%, alongside revised training-budget and averaging reports. PrOntoQA in-distribution prediction accuracy changes from 90.10% to 88.73%. Game24 adds o1-mini at 94% and GPT-4o at 59%, versus FOR at 41%, and removes FOR@100's 65% accuracy and 2.06 diversity.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions expand from unique-parent trees to DAGs with uniform-parent backward probabilities. V3 also explicitly assumes distinct actions produce distinct next states when equating action and transition probabilities. Appendix C.2 introduces the set-based creativity definition in Equations 13–15. The log-variance formulation is retained from v1 Appendix A rather than newly derived.

C1.justification: DAG reasoning changes from future work and an acknowledged tree-only limitation in v1 to a central claimed capability in v3's abstract and introduction. V3 also explicitly claims discovery of solutions absent from competing methods and extends its stated applicability to spatial and abstraction reasoning. The central minimal-data, diversity-seeking training claim remains.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations for program-search failures and attributes GPT-4o/o1-mini's Game24 advantage to stronger reasoning capabilities, including self-verification. Appendix G removes the tree-only limitation and identifies costly trajectory collection and long-horizon reasoning as remaining barriers. These qualify applicability while retaining the main interpretations concerning diverse exploration and generalization.

D1.justification: V3 discloses the separate, greedily decoded Llama-3-8B state-transition model, a 0.5 offset for the zero-augmented-reward ablation, and prompts/settings for the added tasks. It identifies the 1D-ARC transformation-function source and reports training times. Most existing LoRA settings, exploration procedures, A100 hardware information, and code-access disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the new Appendix A substantially expand positioning around divergent thinking, self-correction, inference-time computation, program search, and newer GFlowNet applications. V1's explicit first-work claim is removed. V3 emphasizes higher-level DAG reasoning as its distinction from token-level GFlowNet sequence generation and search-based LLM reasoning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work is split between Section 2 and Appendix A; the log-variance formulation moves into the main method section; and ablations move from the BlocksWorld subsection to Section 4.7. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned around five task panels and a comparative case study, and the appendix BlocksWorld diagram is redrawn as a merged graph. Results tables gain creativity columns, uncertainty entries, and comparator groups; ablations become a separate table. New benchmark, timing, and probability tables are added. Existing prompt tables become styled figures, while Figure 3 is resized, relabeled, and relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central diversity and efficiency claims. V1 lacked evaluated diversity-focused comparators and uncertainty estimates; v3 adds GFN-CoT and diverse-decoding comparisons, repeated-run statistics, diagnostic ablations, and training-cost accounting. The additional tasks test distinct reasoning requirements. These gains outweigh remaining reporting problems, including Section 4.6.1's blanket superiority claim despite Table 5 placing FOR below STaR on in-distribution prediction accuracy.
